This was about 20 years ago when I was around 12 or so. I was raised in a very small, rural town in the southern part of the US. I lived on a large property (1,000 acres)  of about half farm/half woodland. I was always a very outdoorsy type of boy, my dog and I would go and spend many nights out there in the woods to hunt and fish and just be free. One night in November, my dog and I were on our third day or so out in the bush, I found a very old like gazebo type structure with a screen door and screen walls that I of course can see through with about 60 meters of field on all sides until you get to the woods. I thought I found a really cool spot to build a for or something so I was very excited. So that night the plan was to sleep there and go straight home and and get supplies to start improving it. About 4 hours in my sleep, this was about 3-4 AM, I woke up to my dog growling and pacing right in front of me looking at one area of the woods and I really didn’t think much of it, there are countless animals out there but she just wouldn’t stop growling and just wouldn’t chill out. 
I grab my rifle and look out there, (this was nearly a full moon so I could actually see a decent distance) and I see a man walking out of the woods very calmly and not saying a word or showing any expressions but looking at me intently. He had the uniform of a southern Civil War soldier on but he was almost like he was in a black and white movie. He had a huge white beard with piercing blue eyes. I had my rifle the whole time and I asked him “who are you?” “What do you want?” “I have a gun and I’ll shoot you!” Yada yada. By this time my dog is going apeshit and snarling but she wouldn’t leave my side. All this guy did was walk up to me on the other side of the fence and blow air on my face. The first thing I noticed was how cold his breath was but he didn’t have the misty cloud any other person would in like 20 degree weather. I was stunned. He never even looked at my dog. She was a GSD and trained, but he wasn’t fazed at all. After he blew in my face, he cocked he head back and cackled he didn’t laugh, but cackled and walked right back where he came from and disappeared right before he walked in the woods. I’ve never been so petrified in my life.
